title: Exit Interview: first playable of my co-op horde shooter, built with Opus 5.5
author: OptimalPizzas
selftext:
Started this as a test of how far I could get with Claude Code doing basically all the work. I mostly wrote design notes and playtested while a bunch of Opus 5.5 agents built it. About 63 hours start to finish, and maybe 10 of those were me.

It's a top-down horde shooter set in an office that's automating everyone. You herd the robots into the shredder, the mailroom belt and the server vents. Co-op works too, you can invite a friend mid-run.

Stack is three.js, fal + Tripo + Meshy for the main character, Blender scripts for the props, ElevenLabs for the voice and Lyria for the music. Around $29 in generation costs, not counting Claude.

**Biggest lesson so far:** generated 3D looks fine from a high camera and falls apart up close. His glasses squish every time he emotes because it's all one mesh. Curious how others are handling close-ups.

Free to play in the browser (phone works too) if you want to try it: [exitinterview.gg](http://exitinterview.gg)

AMA about the workflow.

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
Hey, Alex here from the Tripo Studio US team. The “looks fine from the gameplay camera, falls apart in close-ups” distinction is really useful.

The glasses squishing during facial motion sounds like exactly the kind of issue where separating accessories from the character mesh could matter a lot.

Are you planning to rebuild the character modularly for close-ups, or are you experimenting with ways to preserve the existing model and just separate/repair the problem areas?

Also, 63 hours for a playable co-op game is kind of wild 😅

replies.author: OptimalPizzas
replies.body:
Thanks for commenting Alex! Given how effectively agents can now A/B test, I’m open to rebuilding the character from the ground up and separating accessories as you suggest.

After some digging, it looks like Tripo’s segmentation workflow isn’t exposed through fal yet. Any update on when that might be supported? Meshy already supports generating separate parts there.
